scenes.tts: Why does your heart slow again after you stop climbing? At the top, your muscles relax, but your heartbeat stays fast. A marker sits above its usual band. Something must move it back without locking it to one value.
scenes.narration: Why does your heart slow again after you stop climbing? At the top, your muscles relax, but your heartbeat stays fast. A marker sits above its usual band. Something must move it back without locking it to one value.
scenes.visual: HOOK WORLD AND COLOUR MAP, carried through both films. A simple full-height human cartoon fills the left half, paused at the top of three stair blocks. A large vertical gauge fills the right half. The usual range is a GOLD band; disturbances are RED; sensor signals are BLUE; control-center signals are YELLOW; responses are TEAL; the current-value marker is WHITE. A small 'schematic' label stays at bottom right. The heart pulses quickly while the stairs slide down and stop. The white marker remains above the gold band and bobs slightly. On the question, a curved return arrow appears but remains unfinished. Nothing freezes.

Title 'When the Body Pushes Back' appears above the carried body and gauge for two seconds. The heart keeps pulsing and the white marker keeps bobbing. The title then fades without resetting the world.

scenes.tts: That shaded band is a range, not a single target. Inside it, the marker can rise and fall. Homeostasis means keeping internal conditions within a stable range while the outside changes. The motion matters more than any one reading.
scenes.narration: That shaded band is a range, not a single target. Inside it, the marker can rise and fall. Homeostasis means keeping internal conditions within a stable range while the outside changes. The motion matters more than any one reading.
scenes.visual: The camera pushes toward the gauge until it fills most of the frame height. The GOLD band widens and receives the label 'stable range'. The white marker settles inside, then drifts gently up and down without leaving. A single-point bullseye briefly appears at the band center, receives a white cross, and dissolves. Outside weather icons for warm and cool slide past behind the gauge.

scenes.tts: Now warm the body. The red disturbance pushes the temperature marker above its band. Sensors in the skin and brain detect that change. They send blue signals to a control center in the brain. The control center sends a yellow command toward sweat glands.
scenes.narration: Now warm the body. The red disturbance pushes the temperature marker above its band. Sensors in the skin and brain detect that change. They send blue signals to a control center in the brain. The control center sends a yellow command toward sweat glands.
scenes.visual: Pull back to the body and gauge. A RED heat field flows toward the body and pushes the white marker above the GOLD band. BLUE dots light in the skin and brain, then travel along blue paths to a YELLOW control-center block inside the head. The yellow block compares a small sensed-marker icon with a gold range icon. A YELLOW pulse travels down to enlarged cartoon sweat glands in a skin inset. TEAL begins only at the sweat.

scenes.tts: Sweat appears on the skin. As it evaporates, heat leaves the skin, and the marker moves toward the band. The response acts against the warming that started it. That direction makes this negative feedback.
scenes.narration: Sweat appears on the skin. As it evaporates, heat leaves the skin, and the marker moves toward the band. The response acts against the warming that started it. That direction makes this negative feedback.
scenes.visual: TEAL sweat drops emerge from the skin inset, shrink into vapor wisps, and carry RED heat arrows upward and away. At the same time, the gauge's white marker glides downward toward the GOLD band. The unfinished return arrow from the hook completes into a loop. A label transforms from 'response' to 'opposes warming', then to 'negative feedback'.

scenes.tts: When internal conditions drift, opposing responses move them toward their range. The condition can still vary inside that range. Negative does not mean harmful here. It means the response pushes against the starting change.
scenes.narration: When internal conditions drift, opposing responses move them toward their range. The condition can still vary inside that range. Negative does not mean harmful here. It means the response pushes against the starting change.
scenes.visual: The body fades slightly while the gauge expands. A RED arrow pushes three different white markers above, below, and inside the GOLD band in sequence. Each outside marker meets a TEAL arrow pointing back toward the band. The inside marker keeps drifting gently. Large text appears briefly: 'response opposes change', while the full rule is not written as subtitles.

scenes.tts: Predict what happens if sweat reaches the skin but cannot evaporate. Does the marker return as quickly, or does it stay higher? Keep the body, range, and sweat in view while you decide.
scenes.narration: Predict what happens if sweat reaches the skin but cannot evaporate. Does the marker return as quickly, or does it stay higher? Keep the body, range, and sweat in view while you decide.
scenes.visual: Restore the hot body, skin inset, and gauge. TEAL sweat drops collect but do not shrink. RED heat arrows remain near the skin. The white marker stays above the GOLD band. A large question appears at top: 'No evaporation: fast return or higher?' Two faint paths extend from the marker, one toward the band and one nearly level.
Deliberate prediction pause. Keep the question and both faint paths. Sweat drops shimmer, heat arrows drift slowly, and the heart pulses. The marker holds nearly still above the GOLD band.

scenes.tts: Without evaporation, sweating removes less heat from the skin. The cooling response is weaker, so the marker stays higher. The response exists, but its effect depends on what happens after the effector acts.
scenes.narration: Without evaporation, sweating removes less heat from the skin. The cooling response is weaker, so the marker stays higher. The response exists, but its effect depends on what happens after the effector acts.
scenes.visual: The downward faint path fades. The nearly level path brightens WHITE, and the marker follows it only slightly downward. A comparison ghost appears beside it: evaporating drops carry red heat away and a ghost marker reaches the band. Label the sweat gland 'effector'. A TEAL response arrow reaches the gland, then becomes thinner after it.

scenes.tts: We can map this loop as change, sensor, control center, effector, and opposing response. Sweat glands are the effectors here. Other body loops may combine parts or spread them across organs. The map is useful, but it is not anatomy for every case.
scenes.narration: We can map this loop as change, sensor, control center, effector, and opposing response. Sweat glands are the effectors here. Other body loops may combine parts or spread them across organs. The map is useful, but it is not anatomy for every case.
scenes.visual: The carried world rearranges into a wide clockwise path without cutting away. The RED heat field becomes 'change'; BLUE skin and brain dots become 'sensor'; the YELLOW head block becomes 'control center'; the TEAL sweat gland becomes 'effector'; evaporation becomes 'opposing response'. Each object stays pictorial and transforms in place. Then the boxes slide closer together to show that parts can be combined.

scenes.tts: A house thermostat follows a similar path: sense, compare, act. A body is richer. Many sensors and effectors work together, and most responses are graded. No one sets a dial inside you.
scenes.narration: A house thermostat follows a similar path: sense, compare, act. A body is richer. Many sensors and effectors work together, and most responses are graded. No one sets a dial inside you.
scenes.visual: The loop path compresses into a large house thermostat cartoon beside the body. Its three labels read 'sense', 'compare', and 'act'. The thermostat switches sharply between off and on. The body replaces it, showing several BLUE sensors and several TEAL response arrows of different thicknesses. The dial icon fades while the body's graded arrows continue moving.

scenes.tts: A correction also takes time. Heart rate does not snap to rest when climbing ends. Signals change, and the rate falls fastest at first. Then it approaches its resting range more gradually.
scenes.narration: A correction also takes time. Heart rate does not snap to rest when climbing ends. Signals change, and the rate falls fastest at first. Then it approaches its resting range more gradually.
scenes.visual: Return to the stair-top body and heart-rate gauge from the hook. The white marker follows a large curve marked 'schematic': steep downward first, then flattening toward a GOLD resting band. The heart pulse slows smoothly with the marker. No numbers appear. The curve and moving marker fill most of the frame.

scenes.tts: Use the simulation to test this map one step at a time. Then a second film compares cases beyond this complete loop.
scenes.narration: Use the simulation to test this map one step at a time. Then a second film compares cases beyond this complete loop.
scenes.visual: The complete loop stretches into five large stepping stones: change, sensor, control center, effector, and response. A white marker moves across them one at a time. Four silhouette tiles slide in behind the gauge: heart, leaf, root, and cell. They remain unlabelled except for a small 'compare next' tag.

End card. Dim the moving body-and-gauge world but keep the heart pulsing and marker drifting. Show one large centered line only, with no smaller line: 'When internal conditions drift, opposing responses move them toward their range.'
